Silver ETF Inflows Surge to Record High

By Jane Doe, Kitco News, September 1, 2026

Silver-backed exchange-traded funds recorded their largest weekly inflow on record this week, as investors piled into the metal amid growing expectations of looser monetary policy. Holdings across the major silver ETFs rose by more than eleven hundred metric tons over five trading sessions, according to data compiled by industry trackers.

Analysts attributed the surge to a combination of factors: a weaker dollar, falling real yields, and renewed industrial demand tied to solar panel manufacturing. Silver, unlike gold, draws roughly half of its annual demand from industrial applications, which has made it especially sensitive to shifts in manufacturing sentiment.

"We have not seen inflows of this magnitude since the early days of the pandemic-era rally," said one commodities strategist at a major bank who was not authorized to speak publicly. "Retail and institutional investors both appear to be positioning for a sustained move higher."

The rush into ETFs came alongside a broader rally in physical silver prices, which climbed more than four percent over the same period to reach levels not seen in over a decade. Trading volumes on futures exchanges also picked up sharply, with open interest in the most active contract rising for a sixth consecutive session.

Market participants will be watching upcoming inflation data and the next central bank policy meeting for further signals on the direction of precious metals prices in the coming weeks. Some analysts caution that a sudden reversal in the dollar could quickly unwind recent gains.
